summary: Elaborates the SNMP administrative model, giving a unified conceptual basis for administering SNMP protocol entities, including authentication, privacy and access control. It is historic, from the party-based SNMP security approach.

eli5.summary: Rules for deciding which network helper may ask which device about what, and who has to prove who they are first.

subtitle: Party-based security framework for administering SNMP management operations.

tldr.problem: SNMP needed a way to define which management stations could perform which operations on which devices, with support for authentication and encryption, going beyond simple community strings.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1351 defines SNMP parties as execution contexts with specific authentication protocols, privacy settings, and MIB views. Messages between parties carry authentication and privacy information, and access control policies govern what each party can do.
tldr.outcome: This party-based security model was published as a historic document; it was later superseded by the user-based security model (USM) in RFC 3414, which became the standard SNMP security approach.

facts.label: Authentication options
facts.value: noAuth or a specific authentication protocol

facts.label: Privacy options
facts.value: noPriv or a specific privacy protocol

today: RFC 1351 is marked historic because it describes the party-based security model, which was superseded by the User-based Security Model (USM) defined in RFC 3414. While the party-based approach was innovative, the user-based model became the standard for SNMP security in practice.

sections.title: Moving Beyond Community Strings
sections.content:
The original SNMP community model identified management participants using simple shared strings (community names). RFC 1351 presents an elaborated administrative model based on the concept of SNMP parties, which unambiguously identify the source and intended recipient of each message.

By using distinct identities for peers and specifying what each identity can do, the model improves on the earlier community scheme. It supports effective access control and allows for future use of asymmetric public-key security protocols.
sections.eli5: Instead of everyone using the same password, each person has their own name and password, and you can say exactly what each person is allowed to do.

sections.title: SNMP Parties and Roles
sections.content:
An SNMP party is a conceptual execution context with a unique identity, an authentication protocol and parameters, a privacy protocol and parameters, and a MIB view defining which objects the party can access.

When a party acts as a management station, it initiates management operations by sending SNMP messages. When a party acts as an agent, it responds to management requests by performing operations on its MIB view. A proxy party forwards requests to remote agents, allowing unmanageable devices to be accessed through SNMP.
sections.eli5: Think of a party as a person with a badge, a secret key and a list of the file drawers they are allowed to open.

sections.title: Authentication and Privacy
sections.content:
Each SNMP party is configured with an authentication protocol that proves the origin and integrity of messages. The party stores private and public authentication keys as needed by its configured protocol. If a party has no authentication protocol (noAuth), its messages are not authenticated.

Each party also has a privacy protocol that protects received messages from disclosure through encryption. The party holds the private and public privacy keys needed by its protocol. Messages can be layered: an authenticated message can be wrapped with privacy protection, giving both integrity and confidentiality.
sections.eli5: Authentication is like signing your name, so people know it is really you. Privacy is like putting a letter in an envelope so nobody can read it on the way.

sections.title: Managing Who Can Do What
sections.content:
An SNMP access control policy specifies which management communication classes (Get, Set, Trap, GetNext, GetResponse) are authorized between pairs of parties. Each policy entry grants a subject party certain privileges when communicating with a target party.

Access to individual MIB objects is determined implicitly: since each party operates on exactly one MIB view, defining what a subject party can do with a target party effectively grants access to the target's MIB view. This design eliminates the need for separate per-object access rules.
sections.eli5: The access policy is like a guard who checks both your ID and your purpose, then lets you to the drawers you are allowed to open.

sections.title: Configuration Scenarios
sections.content:
RFC 1351 describes several deployment configurations. In a non-secure minimal agent, all parties use noAuth and noPriv, equivalent to the original community model. A secure minimal agent adds authentication and privacy.

Proxy configurations allow a management station to reach devices through intermediate proxies. Foreign proxy parties manage devices that use non-SNMP protocols, while native proxy parties forward between SNMP entities. The architecture maintains transparency: the management station need not know whether it is speaking directly to an agent or through a proxy.
sections.eli5: Some offices have no locks (non-secure), some require a key card (secure), and some have a receptionist (proxy) who fetches information from other buildings.
